mentions.name: Fountain pen handwriting practice
mentions.description: A personal hobby of practicing and improving handwriting with different fountain pens, centered on discovering that a 0.6 mm italic nib from Manuscript's Creative Calligraphy set suits small handwriting, since stub/italic/calligraphy nibs create line variation through nib angle rather than pressure. It documents the hard-won lesson that suitable stub nibs below 1 mm are hard to find outside that set.
mentions.problem: Finding a stub/italic nib below 1 mm suited to small handwriting is difficult, and it took a few hundred dollars of experimenting with different nib sizes to learn that stroke width variation comes from pressure and parallel pulling, not the angle-based variation needed.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Handwriting with different fountain pens.

I discovered that a relatively inexpensive 0.6 mm italic nib from Manuscript's Creative Calligraphy set works well with my natural handwriting, it looks "good" even when I'm just starting out.
